name: Peoples of the Pampas, Patagonia and the southern Andes
summary: The Mapuche of Chile, who resisted the Inca and the Spanish for centuries, and the peoples of the Pampas and Patagonia, such as the Tehuelche, Selk’nam and Yaghan. Monte Verde in Chile is one of the oldest human sites in the Americas.
borderNames: Patagonian shellfish and marine mammal hunters

knownFor.label: Cueva de las Manos
knownFor.note: A cave in Patagonia with hundreds of painted hand stencils.

knownFor.label: Mapuche silverwork
knownFor.note: Silver jewellery, a symbol of Mapuche identity.

knownFor.label: Bolas
knownFor.note: Weighted cords thrown to catch guanacos and rheas.

location.value: The Mapuche live in south-central Chile and south-western Argentina. Their homelands once ran from the Choapa Valley to Chiloé, and they later moved east to the pampa and Patagonia.

terrain.value: Andes mountains, grassland, steppe and cold coasts.

climate.value: Temperate to cold; windy in Patagonia.

resources.value: Guanaco, rhea, shellfish, sea lions, farmland in Chile.

population.value: Historian José Bengoa estimated the Mapuche between the Itata River and Reloncaví Sound at 705,000–900,000 in the mid-1500s.

migration.value: Mapuche influence spread east into the Pampas (18th century).

economicBase.value: The traditional Mapuche economy is based on agriculture, with livestock herding; after Spanish contact they adopted wheat, sheep and horses.

tradeRoutes.value: Exchange across the Andes; later horse and cattle trade.

wealth.value: Wealth in horses and cattle after 1600.

inequality.value: Mostly equal communities; leaders gained wealth through trade.

governmentType.value: Extended families under a lonko (chief). The page does not define lof.

keyRulers.value: Lautaro and Caupolicán (Mapuche leaders against Spain).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

succession.value: Leaders chosen for ability and lineage.

institutions.value: Councils (parlamentos) that made treaties with Spain.

armyAndTech.value: Mounted warriors with lances after adopting horses.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

majorWars.value: The Arauco War against Spain (sieges 1550–1598, then low-level conflict for nearly 350 years); Chile and Argentina resumed their campaigns in 1881, and the Mapuche were defeated in 1883.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.value: Kept independence south of the Biobío River for about 300 years.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

inventions.value: Bolas, guanaco-hide cloaks, canoes in the far south.

communicationTransport.value: On foot, later horses; canoes in the southern channels.

religion.value: The machi, usually a woman, leads ceremonies for curing disease and warding off evil.

languageWriting.value: Mapudungun (about 200,000 fluent speakers in Chile, a recent estimate).
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

dailyLife.value: Mapuche rukas (houses of wood and straw); hide tents (toldos) in Patagonia; potatoes, maize, guanaco meat.

neighbours.value: The Inca, the Spanish, later Chile and Argentina.

colonisation.value: Conquered by Chile and Argentina; the Mapuche were defeated in 1883 and Chile completed its occupation in 1884.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

riseSignals.value: Adapted to many environments; horses brought new power.

peakPeriod.value: The Mapuche stayed independent until the late 1800s; the Arauco War lasted nearly 350 years and Chile occupied the lands south of the Biobío in 1884. The Parliament of Quilín is not mentioned.

declineSignals.value: Military campaigns by Chile and Argentina.

outcome.value: The Mapuche are Chile’s largest Indigenous people, with 1,623,073 people in 2024 (about 77% of Chile’s Indigenous population).
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Mapuche; Wikipedia: Tehuelche people (checked 10 Nov 2026)

overallCertainty.value: Known from archaeology and Spanish records.
